findings.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned
findings.body:
In production the flusher creates processes with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False and `process.kill()` is never called.

The old code called `kill()` unconditionally. Now, when a process is detected as hung (`cause = "hang"`), a new process is started for the same shards while the old one keeps running. Two flushers then work the same Redis shards concurrently, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments and leaks a process on every restart.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or test for `threading.Thread` instead.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawned processes
findings.body:
`join()` has the same `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check as the restart path. It is always False for `SpawnProcess`, so `terminate()` is never called on flusher processes that are still alive after the deadline. With N processes per consumer, any that do not exit in time keep running and flushing until the parent process exits.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`.

findings.title: join() stops handling remaining processes once the deadline passes
findings.body: When the deadline is exceeded, the loop `break`s. Every process after that point is neither waited on nor terminated, so on a slow shutdown some flusher processes are left running. Only the waiting should be skipped after the deadline; termination of each remaining process should still happen.

findings.title: Test sleep is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the start. The later `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to "give flusher threads time to process after drift change", therefore does nothing. The test relies on the flusher thread winning a race before `join()` sets the stopped flag, which makes it flaky. Fix: capture the original sleep before patching, or poll for the expected message with a timeout.

findings.title: CLI default contradicts the factory/flusher default of one process per shard
findings.body: `SpanFlusher` treats `max_processes=None` as "one process per shard", and the PR description says the flusher should spawn a process per shard. However, the `--flusher-processes` CLI option defaults to 1. Every consumer started through the CLI will therefore keep a single flusher process unless the flag is passed explicitly, so the advertised scaling is not enabled by default.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name ("shards" vs "shard")
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while the neighbouring `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` metrics use `shard`. Dashboards that filter or group by one tag name will miss the other metric.
